summary:
Risk check of the W1/W2 files at ~22:45Z, 27 Sep. All are files only; nothing was submitted, pushed or committed.
GO:
- W1: exp78b (00:05Z), exp79a (CI slot, ~00:06Z) and exp78a (00:50Z). All three pass their dummies with 0 error markers. Their CSVs differ from each other and from every other dummy (no byte-identical duplicate). All ran under 1,900 s. Their datasets are K2's, plus the unchanged yuki0731 CI dataset (10 files, 2026-08-25).
- W2a: both candidates now have PASSING dummies. exp81 (N2): 1,250 s, SHA 7029fe69, 121,085 nodes (-0.14%). exp80a: 1,388 s, 121,252 nodes, 116 forks. exp81 replaces exp79d as the SEC file.
NO-GO (superseded, not unsafe): exp75, exp76a, exp72, exp76d and exp79d. exp76e is filler only.
Runtime:
- Cap rungs: about 7.5-7.8 h; the knobs add about 0.
- CI files: the model gives 9.4-10.6 h. The code caps CI at 10.75 h, and the worst case is about 10.9 h, below the 12 h limit. Coverage may drop to about 95% of videos at the top of the range.
ERROR modes:
- CI: the only unbounded one is main-process RAM at hidden scale with two CI workers (untested, judged low). Everything else in CI fails soft.
- SEC files: they ERROR only if the private dataset is not attached; K2 #37 proves owner-dataset attachment works. The mount-layout variance only adds about 0.1 h through the rglob fallback.
New read rule (zero cost): the CI stage is invisible on the hidden run, and a fail-soft CI would reproduce exp70g byte for byte. So code a CI file '?' (never '0') when L_hi <= base L_hi + 0.5 h.
Freeze rule: do not delete or change our datasets until all submissions are COMPLETE.
Nothing new reaches R8.

findings.what: Runtime of the CI files on the hidden set is bounded well under 12 h, but the 10.5 h CI deadline may bind at the top of the range. Model: CI stage = N videos x mean s/video / 2 workers = (100-130) x (150-158 s) / 2 = 2.1-2.9 h. The K2 part takes about 7.3-7.7 h of kernel time, so CI ends at about 9.4-10.6 h. Hard bound: workers skip any video whose estimate (1.25 x the slowest video so far) would cross 37,800 s after KERNEL_START_TS, and the main process kills them at 38,700 s (10.75 h). The CSV rewrite takes about 1-2 min on 3-4 M nodes (2 s on 121 k nodes in the dummy) and cells 9-14 take minutes, so the worst case is about 10.9 h. Coverage: 100% at the median, and about 95% of videos refined in the top corner.
findings.evidence: exp79a cell 0 defines KERNEL_START_TS. Cell 8 contains coordinject_run: deadline_ts = kernel_start + 37800, skip-all if start > deadline - 600, kill at deadline + 900. Per-video worker times (dets): 111.3 s (27 k), 70.9 (9 k), 199.1 (58 k), 230.4 (81 k), i.e. t ~ 52 s + 0.00228 s/det. Hidden-video count of 100-130 from CONTEXT l.14. Hidden L for the base: exp70g (7.49, 7.67], exp70q (7.64, 7.81] (experiments/lb_poll/ledger.md). All videos are 100x64x256x256 uint16 (199 train + 4 test zarr.json).
findings.action: No change. Expected completion for exp79a submitted at about 00:06Z: roughly 09:40-10:50Z 28 Sep, still in time for the W2b 12:00Z decision. Keep the CI ledger rule (L_hi <= 10.75 h; 'v' if L_hi > 10.2 h).

findings.what: Read rule that uses latency to tell whether CI ran (costs nothing). A hidden-run log is invisible to us. If the CI stage fails soft on the hidden run (dataset missing, a worker crash on every video, deadline skip), exp79a's CSV becomes byte-identical to exp70g. It would then read 0.956 with 0 teams passed and be mis-coded '0', which would close the CI lever by mistake. The ledger latency shows which case happened: a working CI stage adds 2.1-2.9 h (R21RK-3), while a no-op adds about 0. Proposed rule for exp79a and any CI stack: if L_hi(CI file) <= L_hi(base) + 0.5 h (about <= 8.2 h for exp70g), code it '?' ('CI did not run'), never '0'. If L_hi >= L_hi(base) + 1.2 h, CI ran and the v3 codes apply. Anything in between is '?'. Expected gain: it prevents a false CI closure. P(no-op) is roughly 2-5% (the dataset was checked; the per-video OOM path is fail-soft). The loss it avoids is the W2b CI stack slot.
findings.evidence: Fail-soft paths in exp79a cell 8: a try/except around coordinject_run leaves submission.csv unchanged ('COORDINJECT FAILED'); 'COORDINJECT SKIPPED (deadline)/(no GPU)'; per-video exceptions give 'COORDINJECT_WORKER FAILED' and continue. Dummy CI stage 412-445 s on 4 videos. Base L: exp70g (7.49, 7.67].
findings.action: Add one line to the read card before the exp79a read (~09:40Z): 'CI ran iff L_hi >= base L_hi + 1.2 h; <= base + 0.5 h -> ? (no-op), never 0'. Gate = the ledger at read time; no slot and no GPU needed.

findings.what: The main-process RAM on a ~100-video hidden run while two CI worker subprocesses each load a full video has never been tested. Every dummy had 4 videos, and no log records RSS. An OOM kill of the main process would ERROR the submission; an OOM inside a worker only skips that video (fail-soft). Each worker holds one 100x64x256x256 uint16 video (0.84 GB raw, about 1.7 GB as float32) plus 4 detectors and 2 refiners. Main-process state at the hidden scale is unknown but has to hold ~3 M K2 nodes. I judge this low (<~5%), and it is the only ERROR mode for exp79a I cannot bound from the files.
findings.evidence: grep for RSS / memory / GiB in _dl/biohub-exp79a-k2cap6-coordinject log: 0 hits. Worker env = os.environ with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES = i and OMP_NUM_THREADS = 2; stems split [i::2].
findings.action: No pre-W1 action is possible without a new dummy (a 100-video dummy does not exist). Accept the risk under aggressive mode. If exp79a ERRORs, apply the existing rule (an ERRORed single gets one unchanged resubmit only if its ERROR latency is < 10 h and a slot would otherwise be empty; an ERROR at > 10 h means a timeout or late OOM, so no resubmit and no CI stack). Record the ERROR latency in the ledger.

findings.what: SEC files (exp81, exp79d, exp72, exp76d) have one hard-ERROR path and one slow path. Hard ERROR: cell 3 raises FileNotFoundError at module level (not fail-soft) if no ARTIFACT_MANIFEST.json with the expected weight_sha256 exists under /kaggle/input. That happens only if the private dataset is not attached at the rerun. Owner-dataset attachment on a hidden rerun is already proven by K2 #37 (vitaliineibauer/biohub-ft-weights), so this risk is below 1%. Slow path: Kaggle mounts datasets in two layouts, and 27 Sep dummies showed both. In the old layout (/kaggle/input/<slug>) the explicit manifest path misses and the code falls back to rglob over /kaggle/input. That cost ~210 s on the visible run; with ~100 hidden videos x 102 zarr files it is at most ~+50%. So about +0.06-0.1 h of latency, and no ERROR.

findings.what: The cap rungs are not duplicates, but on a low-eligible (44b6-like) video they are nearly the same file: the frame cap binds at 7-8 insertions. On dummy video 44b6_0113 (14 eligible), cap 6 / cap 8 / cap 12 fc2 / cap 24 fc2 add 6 / 7 / 8 / 8. On the high-eligible 6bba videos (33 and 142 eligible) they add 6/8/12/21 and 6/8/12/24. exp78a is therefore nested inside exp78b's increment: +1/0/+2/+2 over exp70g, against +2/0/+6/+6. If the public embryo looks like 44b6, all three rungs sit within about +2 insertions per video of exp70g, and '0' reads say little about private. This is already covered by R20-A2's stop rules; it adds no new slot.

The fallbacks exp75, exp76a (1,896 s), exp72 and exp76d are NO-GO because they are superseded, not because of runtime: exp79a and exp81 passed on the stronger cap-6 base. exp76e is filler only; 46 (cap 6 + thr 0.3 + forkmid) already read '0', and exp76e is nested in it.
